title: One-step extraction and analysis of 45 contaminants of emerging concern using QuEChERS methodology and HR-MS in radish leaves and roots
author: Labad, Montemurro, et al.

steps.title: Collect and store radish tissue
steps.instruction: Hand‑wash whole radish plants, separate roots from leaves, place each tissue in a labelled container and freeze at –20 °C for 48 h.

steps.title: Lyophilize, grind and store powder
steps.instruction: Lyophilize the frozen tissues, grind them to a fine powder with a knife mill, and store the powder at –20 °C until extraction.

steps.title: Hydrate sample and add internal standard
steps.instruction: Weigh 1 g of lyophilized powder into a 50 mL polypropylene centrifuge tube, add 9 mL water, vortex 2 min, let stand 1 h; add 50 µL of a standard mixture (2 µg mL⁻¹ in MeOH) to obtain a final concentration of 10 ng g⁻¹, vortex 5 min and let stand another 1 h.

steps.title: Extract with solvent and QuEChERS salts
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL extraction solvent (as defined for the matrix), vortex 2 min, add the appropriate QuEChERS salt (original non‑buffered salts for roots, CEN 15662 buffered salts for leaves), hand‑shake to avoid MgSO₄ agglomerates and vortex again.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect organic layer
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube 10 min at 4000 rpm and 4 °C, transfer the top organic layer to a glass tube and store overnight at –20 °C to precipitate fatty acids, proteins, chlorophyll and sugars.

steps.title: Skip cleanup and prepare final extract
steps.instruction: For the selected methods (method 3 for roots and method 5 for leaves) omit the dSPE cleanup: after the overnight –20 °C step, aspirate 1 mL of the organic layer, transfer it directly to an HPLC glass vial, evaporate to dryness under a gentle N₂ stream and re‑constitute in 1 mL 10 % MeOH.

substeps.instruction: If a cleanup were performed (methods 1, 3, 5, 7), 6 mL of the organic phase would be transferred to a PSA‑containing tube containing 900 mg MgSO₄, 150 mg PSA and 150 mg C₁₈, hand‑shaken 30 s, vortexed 2 min, centrifuged 5 min at 4000 rpm and 4 °C, and 1 mL of the supernatant would be taken for further processing.

steps.title: LC‑MS/MS injection parameters
steps.instruction: Inject 10 µL of the re‑constituted extract using an autosampler set at 8 °C; separate on a Hibar® HR Purospher® STAR RP‑C18 column (100 mm × 2.1 mm i.d., 2 µm) maintained at 40 °C; flow rate 0.5 mL min⁻¹; mobile phase A (positive mode) = 5 mM ammonium acetate with 0.1 % formic acid, B = ACN; mobile phase A (negative mode) = 2 mM ammonium fluoride in water, B = ACN; gradient: 0.0 min 5 % B, 0.33 min 5 % B, 6.33 min 40 % B, 10.33 min 96 % B, 11.16 min 96 % B, 13.16 min 5 % B; total run time 13 min.

steps.title: Mass spectrometer source settings
steps.instruction: Set ion spray voltage to +5500 V (positive) and –4500 V (negative); source temperature 550 °C; nitrogen gas flow 55 psi; curtain gas 30 psi; collision gas (CAD) 7 psi; TOF‑MS survey range 100–950 Da with 120 ms accumulation time; declustering potential 80 V (+) / –80 V (–); collision energy 10 V (+) / –10 V (–).

steps.title: Mass calibration during batch
steps.instruction: Automatically recalibrate the instrument by infusing reserpine (C₃₃H₄₀N₂O₉, m/z 609.2807) for (+)ESI or a sodium‑trifluoroacetate cluster (TFA‑Na)₅+TFA⁻ at m/z 792.8596 for (–)ESI; the system provides a resolving power of 31 000–44 000 at m/z 132.9049 and 829.5395 with a mass error of 0.4 ppm.

steps.title: Perform method validation – spiking
steps.instruction: Prepare spiked samples at five levels (2, 5, 10, 50 and 200 ng g⁻¹) in triplicate (n = 3), add the internal‑standard mixture, process them through steps 3–6, and calculate recoveries as the ratio of peak area in spiked matrix extract to peak area in a blank matrix extract spiked at the same level.

steps.title: Assess intra‑day precision
steps.instruction: Repeat the recovery experiment five times (n = 5) for each spiking level and compute the relative standard deviation (RSD %); accept precision values < 20 % for most compounds.

steps.title: Determine LOD and LOQ
steps.instruction: Determine the limit of detection (LOD) as the lowest concentration giving a signal‑to‑noise ratio > 3; determine the limit of quantification (LOQ) as the lowest concentration giving S/N > 10 and RSD ≤ 20 %, using matrix‑matched calibration curves.

steps.title: Evaluate matrix effect
steps.instruction: Extract blank radish matrix (n = 3), spike at the same levels as the recovery study, and compare peak areas to those of standards prepared in 90 % H₂O/10 % MeOH (v/v); calculate %ME and consider |ME| > 40 % as significant matrix influence.

steps.title: Create matrix‑matched calibration curve
steps.instruction: Prepare a calibration series in blank radish matrix with at least eight concentration points ranging from 0.05 to 300 ng mL⁻¹ (dry weight), inject and plot response; accept the curve when the coefficient of determination r² ≥ 0.99.

steps.title: Apply method to cultivated radish
steps.instruction: Sow 4 radish seeds per pot (6 pots total), grow 5 days, then irrigate every 2 days for 20 days with 200 mL artificial contaminated water containing 10 ng g⁻¹ of target CECs (control pots receive tap water); after 21 days harvest, hand‑wash, separate roots and leaves, freeze at –20 °C for 48 h, lyophilize, grind to powder and analyse following steps 3–6.
